turns.content: For two uncoupled nuclei in a strong magnetic field, explain how the joint product-state basis is constructed from the individual magnetic quantum states.
State the product-state counting rule and the single-spin-flip selection rule that will be applied.
Now take both nuclei to have spin 1/2 and list their combined spin product states.
The two nuclei have different magnetic shieldings. Explain what this implies for the product-state energies listed above.
Apply the rule that one spin flips while the other remains fixed to enumerate the allowed transitions.
Report the ordered pair of level count and transition count and list the allowed connections.
Explain why not every pairwise connection between the product-state levels is allowed.
